newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa reverses to end up, aided by strong NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa reverses to end up, aided by strong NY.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures erased its morning losses in the afternoon to end higher, on the heels of a stronger-than-expected New York open.
July closed up 21 stg at 1,018 stg per tonne and September up 18 at 1,033. Volume picked up after a lacklustre morning to tally 4,713 trades for the day.
New York's lead in the rally was reflected in the narrower arbitrage spread to about 90 from about 100 last week, traders said.
Some attributed New York's strength to a local short-squeeze, but others said New York's gains stemmed from talk the Ivory Coast mid-crop would not be as good as expected due to poor quality beans.
Traders said the lowest estimates they had heard stood near 100,000 tonnes. That compares with some early forecasts between 160,000 and 180,000 tonnes and an average closer to 150,000 tonnes.
Some traders also said there was some market nervousness about weather patterns suggesting dry weather could hit Brazil and Africa.

Technically, traders said the market was ripe for a move up after lagging New York cocoa and wallowing aimlessly near the bottom end of its trading range. They said the lack of momentum to break through serious support levels made cocoa vulnerable to an upswing.
But even with the afternoon rise, July still failed to score the week's high by two stg. July's weekly high was set on Monday at 1,019.
In London's afternoon run up, traders noted some industry and speculative buying. But cocoa's rise was met by origin sales, they said.

In the morning, activity was sluggish as July held to a three-stg range. Crosses dominated early with one firm crossing 500 March contracts and a French firm crossing about 270 May 1998 contracts, traders said.
Options activity picked up with futures. Seventy July 1,100 stg calls and 1,000 stg puts traded and 50 September 1,100 stg calls changed hands.
